walkthroughs.body_html:
The atomic model has been rebuilt many times: Dalton → Thomson → Rutherford → Bohr → modern.

Dalton said atoms were tiny solid spheres. Thomson found the electron and drew the plum pudding: a positive blob with electrons stuck in it.

Rutherford's team fired alpha particles at thin gold foil. Most went straight through. A few were deflected. A tiny number bounced right back.

This proved the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus. Bohr then said electrons orbit in fixed shells.

Elements are mixtures of isotopes. The relative atomic mass is the weighted mean of their masses.

Formula: RAM = (mass1 x %1 + mass2 x %2) / 100. For chlorine: (35 x 75 + 37 x 25) / 100 = 35.5.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
